primary_object_card.object_statement: A finite Type-1 and Type-2 bidirectional science loop tests the same four projection object cards by alternating candidate, measurement, counter-projection, update, falsifier, and receipt steps, then compares which object distinctions survive each engine method under held-out and erased controls.

source_anchors.quote_or_summary: Projection battery v0 establishes four finite object cards and five partial MMM-style views with erased controls at chance.
Full Type-1/Type-2 64-live v1 establishes the parent finite carrier with two engine sheets, 16 macro rows, and 64 ordered microsteps.
Audit requires per-engine method closure before stronger QIT, perception, ontology, or Lev mesh claims.

primary_object_card.plain_language_definition: A bounded finite experiment where Type-1 and Type-2 are treated as two different scientific methods over the same four object cards. Each method must propose a candidate, measure a view, perform the opposite-direction counter-projection, update the candidate, run a falsifier, and emit a receipt. The object is the method loop plus its comparison table, not the engine labels, not live perception, and not a Lev mesh object.

native_terms.Type-1 method: The finite method that starts from object-to-view prediction and is tested by whether the predicted measurement survives a counter-projection back to object identity.
native_terms.Type-2 method: The finite method that starts from view-to-object counter-projection and is tested by whether the recovered object predicts held-out measurement structure.
native_terms.bidirectional science: A loop that must run both forward prediction and backward reconstruction before emitting a receipt, with falsifiers attached to both directions.
native_terms.counter-projection: The opposite-direction readout used to test whether a candidate survives more than one projected vocabulary or measurement surface.

weirdness_signature: the same object family is tested by two opposite method orders
success requires a receipt after both a prediction and a counter-projection
Type-1 and Type-2 may have different strengths without either becoming the whole object
primary_object_card.domain: four finite projection object cards, five finite projection views, Type-1 and Type-2 method orders, and explicit erased or shuffled controls
primary_object_card.codomain_or_output: method receipts, per-engine pass/fail metrics, unique-win comparison table, survivor hashes, and blocked-consumer list
allowed_operations: run Type-1 object-to-view prediction then counter-project back to object
run Type-2 view-to-object reconstruction then predict held-out measurement
compare method accuracy and unique-win fields
run erased, shuffled, and label-leak controls
required_invariants: both engine methods use the same four object cards
both engine methods use the same five projection views
each method has candidate, measurement, counter-projection, update, falsifier, and receipt stages
direct loop and engine labels stay blocked as evidence
forbidden_substitutions: perception analogy promoted to live perception
primary_object_card.adapter_policy: JAX, Julia, PyTorch, SMT, Graphs, and torch.func are adapters or probes; they become claim-bearing only when their outputs gate the finite method receipt and fail under erased controls.
promotion_locks: no ontology writer or MMM driver admission

extended_constraints: same object family across Type-1 and Type-2

loop_contract.repair_rule: repair the first object-preservation or evidence-boundary error before adding new method variants
loop_contract.stop_condition: all object-preservation errors pass or a named first-class field cannot be instantiated from the parent receipts

method_contracts.question_is_not_authorization: A question asks for an answer; it is not authorization to implement unless the user explicitly says to do it.
method_contracts.order_check_separate: Any sequence or ordering claim must be checked separately from content correctness, with the order witness named.
method_contracts.baseline_preservation: When debugging runtime behavior, preserve the tuned visible/output baseline and debug the execution path underneath.
method_contracts.falsifier_first: A Popper pass names the target claim, strongest live falsifier, decisive check, and killed/open/survived classification before agreement.
method_contracts.feynman_testability: A Feynman pass names the operation, the observable measured, and the pass/fail condition.
method_contracts.synthesis_refusal: Synthesis must name distinct receipts and explicitly refuse the merge, sequence, or reframe it is not performing.
method_contracts.human_offload: Resolve with tools before asking; ask the human only for private, preference-bound, or unrecoverable information.
